evidence_quotes.quote: Se aplicaron dos encuestas con dos muestreos aleatorios estratificados (Mukherjee et al., 2022) a una población finita de 88,686 usuarios del SEAPAL-VALLARTA (SEAPAL, 2023).

El primer muestreo a usuarios domésticos, doméstico residencial, Comerciales e Industriales (D.C.I.) y el segundo, a usuarios hoteleros con una muestra de 364 usuarios D.C.I. y 100 usuarios hoteleros.

Los artículos 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 46, 51 y 58 del RPSPAPDATDARMPV establecen contribuciones y pagos de derechos que deberá realizar la población para solicitar la contratación de los servicios, cubrir las cuotas por la conexión a las redes e instalación de tomas y dictamen de factibilidad, así como la adhesión al contrato con el organismo operador para la prestación de los servicios.

La asequibilidad de las tarifas se promueve a su vez con las disposiciones del capítulo VII del RPSPAPDATDARMPV, que establecen subsidios para instituciones de asistencia social y uso doméstico, sin que estos rebasen el 50% de los costos del consumo y previo el cumplimiento de requisitos correspondientes, como se señala en la tabla 4.
Aun cuando el 60% de los usuarios D.C.I. manifiestan que el costo es accesible, se tiene al 38% que afirman costos elevados con 137 usuarios en este último porcentaje

el 66.20% de los usuarios D.C.I. se sienten seguros de contar con agua al hacer el pago por el suministro y 33.80% de estos usuarios afirman que dicho pago no les asegura el poder disponer del recurso hídrico.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines drinking water and wastewater sanitation service access, affordability, and supply security among municipal utility (SEAPAL-VALLARTA) user accounts, including domestic and residential domestic households as well as commercial, industrial, and hotel users in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico.
criterion_notes.c2: Passes BOTH the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2. Under the plain reading, it analyzes federal, state, and municipal water legislation and regulation. Under the narrow rule-type reading, it specifically analyzes tariff and cost-recovery rules (minimum quota, increasing block, and total-cost volumetric tariff regimes under Art. 46 and 52 of RPSPAPDATDARMPV and Art. 56 of the 2025 Municipal Revenue Law), connection fees and service-contracting requirements (Arts. 4, 9, 14, 16, 18, 44, 57, and 58 of RPSPAPDATDARMPV), and eligibility/tenure/documentation rules for domestic tariff subsidies up to 50% (Chapter VII of RPSPAPDATDARMPV, requiring Mexican citizenship, owner or tenant residence, income threshold, payment currency, and bimonthly consumption <= 60 m3).
criterion_notes.c3: Contains primary empirical survey evidence alongside legal-regulatory analysis: two stratified random surveys of SEAPAL-VALLARTA users (n = 364 domestic/commercial/industrial users sampled via QGIS across neighborhoods and n = 100 hotel users from a utility list out of 88,686 registered users), analyzed using descriptive statistics and contingency tables in SPSS 2021.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports empirical outcomes directly relevant to affordability and reliability/availability: approximate user bill payments and tariff-tier distribution (e.g., 89.83% of D.C.I. users in the increasing-cost tier), perceived affordability of water and sanitation tariffs (60% accessible vs. 38% elevated among D.C.I. users; 63% vs. 37% among hotel users), and perceived security of continuous drinking water supply upon paying tariffs (66.20% secure vs. 33.80% insecure among D.C.I. users, compared to 91% vs. 9% among hotel users).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and unit of analysis (registered utility user accounts of SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta: n = 364 D.C.I. users including domestic/residential domestic households and n = 100 hotel users), legal/regulatory exposure (economic valuation in LAN and municipal connection-fee, block-tariff, and subsidy rules in RPSPAPDATDARMPV and Ley de Ingresos 2025), outcomes (tariff expenditure tiers, perceived affordability, and perceived supply security), and study design (cross-sectional socio-legal and stratified random survey study) are all clearly identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with English and Spanish title and abstract). Per Criterion 10, Spanish full text is clean and directly translatable, and the study provides relevant empirical socio-legal evidence on municipal tariff, connection-fee, and subsidy regulation; translation method and translator should be logged in extraction_note during data extraction.

study_design: Cross-sectional socio-legal regulatory analysis and stratified random user survey
population_and_sample: Registered utility user accounts of SEAPAL-VALLARTA in Puerto Vallarta, Jalisco, Mexico (finite population N = 88,686; stratified random samples of n = 364 domestic, residential domestic, commercial, and industrial [D.C.I.] users and n = 100 hotel users)
exposure: Legal economic valuation of water (Ley de Aguas Nacionales) and municipal utility tariff, connection-fee, contracting, and domestic subsidy eligibility rules (RPSPAPDATDARMPV and Ley de Ingresos del Municipio de Puerto Vallarta 2025)
outcome: Approximate water and sanitation tariff payments and volumetric tariff-tier placement, user-perceived tariff affordability, and perceived security/continuity of drinking water supply upon payment
rationale: This socio-legal empirical study satisfies all inclusion criteria (c1-c6). It examines drinking water and wastewater sanitation service access, affordability, and supply security among SEAPAL-VALLARTA utility users in Puerto Vallarta, Mexico (c1). It directly analyzes rule-type legal and regulatory mechanisms governing service access — specifically volumetric tariff regimes (minimum quota, increasing block, and total cost), connection fees and service-contracting rules, and eligibility/tenure/citizenship/consumption rules for up to 50% domestic subsidies under the municipal utility regulation (RPSPAPDATDARMPV) and 2025 Municipal Revenue Law — satisfying both the plain and narrow 2026-10-13 readings of Criterion 2 (c2). It provides primary empirical evidence from two stratified random surveys (n = 364 D.C.I. users including domestic households and n = 100 hotel users) reporting tariff payment brackets, perceived affordability, and perceived supply security upon payment (c3, c4, c5). Although written in Spanish (with an English abstract), full-text translation is directly feasible per Criterion 10 (c6).
